needs: A sorted array being searched: the remaining range shrinks by half at each check.

brief.title: Binary search: finding a number by halving
brief.idea: Binary search finds a value in a sorted list by checking the middle and discarding the half that cannot hold it, so fifteen items need at most four checks.

beats.say: Here are fifteen numbers in order, smallest to largest, and we want to know whether forty seven is one of them.
beats.show: A row of fifteen boxes appears, each holding one number, sorted from 3 on the left to 64 on the right.

beats.say: Checking them one by one could take fifteen looks. Because the list is sorted, we can do far better.
beats.show: A pointer starts stepping box by box from the left, then stops and is removed.

beats.say: Look at the middle box first. It holds thirty four, which is smaller than forty seven.
beats.show: The middle box, holding 34, is highlighted and compared with 47.

beats.say: So forty seven cannot be anywhere on the left. That whole half is gone after one single check.
beats.show: The middle box and the seven boxes to its left are greyed out, leaving seven boxes.

beats.say: In what is left, the middle is fifty one, which is too big, so now the right part goes.
beats.show: Among the remaining seven, the middle box, 51, is highlighted, then it and the three boxes to its right are greyed out.

beats.say: Three boxes remain. The middle one holds forty two, too small, which leaves a single box.
beats.show: Of the three remaining boxes, the middle one, 42, is highlighted, then it and the box to its left are greyed out.

beats.say: That last box holds forty seven. Found, on the fourth check instead of the eleventh.
beats.show: The one remaining box, 47, is marked as the match and a counter reads 4 checks.

beats.say: Each check halved what was left: fifteen boxes, then seven, then three, then one.
beats.show: The four steps are shown one above the other as shrinking rows of 15, 7, 3 and 1 boxes.

beats.say: Double the list and you add only one more check. A million sorted numbers need about twenty.
beats.show: Two lines appear below the rows: 30 items take 5 checks, and one million items take about 20.

beats.say: The one condition is that the list stays sorted. Without the order, throwing away half would be a guess.
beats.show: The row of fifteen is shuffled, and the halving steps beside it are crossed out.
